contract.reader: A C programmer who knows a microcontroller's registers and the superloop (entry 1) and needs peripheral data to reach the program without loss
contract.problem: Choosing between polling, interrupts and DMA for a given input, and writing interrupt code that neither misses deadlines nor corrupts shared data
contract.outcome: Compute polling latency, worst-case interrupt latency and the processor load of interrupt-per-item and DMA handling; follow the ISR rules; recognize races and torn reads; protect shared data with a short critical section or an SPSC ring buffer; set up double buffering and know its deadline and delay; pick a method from the decision table
contract.contribution: One quantitative thread (the 115 200 bit/s UART and its 86.8 us deadline, the 10 kHz ADC) carried through all three methods; a C11 ring buffer with correct acquire/release ordering and real test output; a decision table and four worked design decisions
contract.evidence: Worked arithmetic; the ring-buffer program and load-comparison script with real output; Arm DDI 0403E.e, ISO/IEC 9899:2011, Ganssle (2008), Lee and Seshia (2017), White (2011), Yiu (2014)
contract.limitations: Generic Cortex-M at 48 MHz with invented register names; vendor DMA specifics, multicore concurrency and OS primitives out of scope

findings.location: Section 3.1 sequence diagram; Section 5.2 double-buffering flowchart (mobile-light-27)
findings.problem: Neither Mermaid diagram has a caption; at 360 px the flowchart's last node is cut off with no scroll cue
findings.whyItMatters: A caption tells the reader what to notice and gives the phone reader the cut destination in words
findings.action: Add a one-sentence caption to each diagram; consider flowchart TB so the flowchart fits at 360 px
findings.acceptance: facts.json of new captures reports 0 SVG figures without a title and both diagrams have a caption

findings.problem: At 1280 px the inline code wraps at the hyphen, splitting the -> operator into TIMER- and >COUNT
findings.whyItMatters: The exercise asks the reader to diagnose this exact expression; a split operator reads as a subtraction
findings.action: Keep TIMER->COUNT unbroken (word joiner, code block, or a site-level rule against breaking inline code after a hyphen)
findings.acceptance: On new captures at 1280 and 360 px TIMER->COUNT appears on one line

findings.location: Section 3.5, '11 520 bytes/s' and '100 000 items per second' (mobile-light-16)
findings.problem: Digit-group spaces are breaking spaces, so grouped numbers split across lines at 360 px
findings.whyItMatters: A split number reads as two numbers
findings.action: Non-breaking (narrow) spaces in grouped numbers, preferably by the site-wide step proposed in the Inside a Microcontroller review (L4)
findings.acceptance: Neither split appears on new captures at 360 px
